questions: FOR THE LEAD FIRST, THE RECEDING DIRECTION AT THE SEAM: the nearest ground evidence reads OUTSIDE 31.6 +/- 5 on both sides of the road, in opposite directions. North side (the official hall's stair rails at u 12564-12677, -60/-61; the shop tables at 12952-13253, -51 to -62): mean -57 at u ~12940. South side (the bottom shop's tables, counter and bench at 12663-12907, +77 to +119): mean +97 at u ~12810, agreeing with S4.bld.south_hall_12350's ridge (+92) and part 1's high lines east of 11420 (+84 to +91). East, the tea house group: median -68 at u ~14500 (-36 to -122). The open square's edges (u 13390-13715, the one north-running large line) stand almost upright (-8 to 0, est). Stroke points in derivation. The painter draws each furniture group from its own side, so one dx per u cannot hold both sides. Options, computed (derivation, last item): a ramp inside S4b to either side's value stretches (x2.8 at the road, x8.8 at the silk's top, to -57) or folds (to +97) the plan within 200-340 px; a slow ramp to -57 over all of S4b stretches the top 1.9x and hands S3 -57 against its +46 to +51; re-knotting part 1 moves its built east end 8-35 m (to -57) or folds its top rows (to +97). The frame keeps the constant 31.6 so both seams hold and nothing folds; furniture orientation is then a builder choice. Changing it is one edit of dx_knots and `scroll_map.mjs S4b all` plus `map_layout.mjs S4b`.

THE WATER LEVEL is a bound, not a reading (supports, water): no vertical bank face, stair, revetment or jetty is painted on S4b's moorings, and S3's agents found none in 15500-20650 either. If a later section (S2's wharves, S1) paints a revetment or a stair meeting the water, its two-point reading should replace -0.7 for the whole river, with the lead's agreement.

THE DIMINUTION UP THE SILK (standing figures, painted height against foot v; the evidence for BUILDING.md rule 5): about 170 px on the road (v 1500-1770: 168 at 1768, 163 at 1093), about 150 at the crowd (v 640-690: 146-155, 0.88), 99 at v 490-550 (the youth and the muleteer: 0.58), 57-69 at v 400-406 on the bank (0.35-0.4); seated crew on the boats 38-54 px at v 535-556. Buildings agree (checks): the eaves on the road's edge come out about 2.3-3.1 m, the shop behind the crowd (v 500) 1.5 m, and the top-edge shops (v 150-200) 0.9-1.0 m. Sizes up the silk are builder choices (real size, painted place); the big boat's painted 12 m hull is the same diminution, not a small boat.

THE ROAD EAST OF u 15215 is hidden behind the south row and the willows; structures_w and structures_e both read it bending south-east past the long hall's east gable to (15500, 1530, est, conf low), along the front of S3's riverside hall (reading b). That point is S3's datum (the lead's call for S3: reading c starts at it). If S3's mapping places its road differently, S4b.road.main's last three centre points move with it.

THE FAR BANK AND THE TOP-OF-SILK STRIP: at the one depth rate the far bank's top at v 75-85 lies about 29 m north of the street's datum row and 15 m beyond the near shore at u 15500 (checks). It is painted small (the far-bank willows, the open shed): keep the one-scale frame and settle room at build time (BUILDING.md rule 5).

THE TWO SIDES' FURNITURE IN THE WORLD: with dx 31.6 the shop hall's and tea house's furniture map as parallelograms skewed 49-52 degrees west of north, and the bottom shop's 40 degrees east of north. Builders should place each table, bench and stall by its base point and orient it square to the road (or to its hall) as a recorded choice, not along the mapped skew.

THE FAR BANK'S FACE: with water at -0.7 the far shore's est line (v 112-122, hidden behind the small cabin boat) maps 0.3 m NORTH of the far bank's top (v 75-82, H 0): a far-bank face 0.7 m high, seen from the south, needs its waterline at least 54 px below its top (v >= 129 at u 15500). Either the far shore lies lower on the silk than est (under the boat), or the far bank stands about 0.2-0.5 m below the street. The builder should take the water plane to the far bank_top line and treat the shore there as hidden (choice).
